newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts ease back with Bunds, await BOE report.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts ease back with Bunds, await BOE report.

text.p: UK government bond (gilt) futures eased back in light, early trade as the market awaited the Bank of England's crucial inflation report due at 1030 GMT.
"It's all eyes on the Bank," said one gilt trader at a UK brokerage. "After the governor's comment's yesterday it looks like rates will stay here for a couple of months."
Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Monday that the UK now had a "better or even" chance of meeting the medium-term aim of inflation at 2.5 percent or lower.
By 0718 GMT, LIFFE June gilts were down 6/32 at 114-8/32 whilst June Bunds were 10 basis points weaker at 102-17/32.
"We think the Bank's going to be a little bit more positive about meeting the inflation target now and the market should be able to get through that all right," HSBC bond economist Philip Tyson said.
UK official interest rates were increased by 25 basis points, taking them to 6.25 percent and the central bank was also given the power to decide the level of interest rates from now on.
Market optimism about Britain's ability to hold down inflation has increased and Tyson sees the gilt/Bund spread dipping to 90 basis points by September from 140 at the moment.
"It'll be down to the more positive attitude of Labour towards Europe, there's a better chance of hitting the inflation target and we're expecting a fiscally tight budget in June," he said.

The market is also awaiting details, due at 1430 GMT, of the amount of gilts to be auctioned on May 20 and 22. The central bank has already announced that the stocks will be the 7.0 percent of Treasury stock due 2002 and the 8.0 percent of 2021.
Analysts suggest that the funding position is healthy enough for the authorities to go only for around 3.0 or 4.0 billion stg.
At the short end of the yield curve, LIFFE June short sterling was up one basis point at 93.49 whilst the more active September contract was also one basis point higher at 93.28.
